title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class parallel Pollard rho in GT

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with R=1024 twisted multipliers, a 4-Fp-multiplication canonical-conjugate key and deterministic fruitless-cycle escape; output P=[x]P0 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds with probability at least 0.40 using at most 2^125.89 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000), including setup, pairings, table construction, walk starts, distinguished-point handling, cycle handling, detection delay, output and verification. Peak memory is below 2^73 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^31 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for R-adding rho walks (with the Brent-Pollard R/(R-1) correction and 3% explicit step slack), supported by toy-field experiments; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on real BLS12-381 GT elements, check the Frobenius formula, the 4-multiplication conjugate-key formula, distinctness of the 12 keys, consistency of the canonical representative, p^6 = inversion, ord_r(p)=12. Part B: run the complete Frobenius-class rho walk (kappa trick, twisted table, 2-cycle and checkpoint escapes, distinguished points, collision solving) in a small field with the same tower shape and report collision times against the random-mapping model. Toy scale only; does not validate production costs.
